TOPIC:
Review of the Fiscal Year 2026 Year-End Financial Report and Proposed Commitment of Fund Balance

BACKGROUND:
Pursuant to Virginia Code § 22.1-100, WJCC Schools may not carry forward unexpended funds from one fiscal
year to the next unless the School Board takes action to commit or assign those funds for a specific purpose.

Historically, pursuant to the School Division’s operational contract with the City of Williamsburg and James City
County, 90% of unexpended funds were allocated to the “Future School Use Account”, with the remaining 10%
returned to the localities based on their respective funding shares.

During Fiscal Year 2026, James City County returned a portion of the School Division's Fiscal Year 2025 fund
balance to establish a healthcare reserve fund. Subsequently, both James City County and the City of
Williamsburg expressed support for directing any remaining Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance to the
healthcare reserve fund to help address future healthcare cost obligations and strengthen the Division's long-
term financial position.

RATIONALE:
Administration is recommending that the Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance be committed to the
healthcare reserve fund. This recommendation is supported by both James City County and the City of
Williamsburg and advances the School Division's efforts to build financial capacity to manage future
healthcare-related expenditures.

SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
Revenue and expenditure information presented is preliminary, unaudited, and subject to change.

COST BUDGETED:
N/A

ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation to commit the Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance to the
   healthcare reserve fund.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.

SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board review the information and be prepared to vote on the proposed
commitment of the Fiscal Year 2026 year-end fund balance to the healthcare reserve fund at the September
15, 2026 meeting.

Process
The Teaching & Learning and College, Career and Readiness (CCR) departments will lead the textbook
selection and adoption process for each content area in collaboration with review committees and informed by
stakeholder input. The proposal includes the identification of the textbook evaluation committee, a timeline for
the scope of work, and adherence to the guidelines and criteria outlined in Policy IIAA and Regulation IIAA-R,
for each course.
Committee
Each textbook selection committee will include a school board member, division staff, school administrators,
general education teachers, specialists representing content, special education, multilingual learners, gifted,
parents/guardians, and community members.

School Board Policy IIAA requires the local school board approve the textbook selection and adoption
schedule, the textbook evaluation committee, and evaluation criteria.

items.title: Review Request to Modify and Extend Construction Management Services for Two Pre-K Centers to McDonough Bolyard Peck (MBP)
items.body:
TOPIC:
Review Request to Modify and Extend the contract for Construction Management Services for Two Pre-K
Centers to McDonough Bolyard Peck (MBP) for a Cost of $263,840
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
DJ, Purchasing
DJ-R, Purchasing Regulation
BACKGROUND:
On August 20, 2024 the School Board approved construction management services in the amount of
$554,360. MBP’s contract is based on providing 12 months of construction-phase services for this project.
Construction phase services began on October 1, 2025, and therefore, run through September 30, 2026.
Based on the current schedule provided by Oyster Point Construction Company, MBP is proposing to extend
the construction management services by eight months and change the end date for these services from
September 30, 2026, to May 31, 2027.
Construction management services include support and assistance with:
• An onsite management team for the duration of the project
• A monthly update to the administration on construction progress
• A document review for constructability
• A construction milestone schedule
• Pre-bid and post-bid conferences
• A review of the construction contract
• Recommendations regarding all proposed change-orders
RATIONALE:
N/A
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
As agreed, the construction phase services extended beyond 12 months and the monthly construction phase
fee is $32,980. The additional cost of modification is $263,840. Total cost of the construction management
services is now $818,200. The FY24 and FY25 Capital Improvement Plan included Pre-K Space Construction
and FFE funding in the amounts of $28,778,775 and $6,470,280 respectively.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:



The superintendent recommends the board review the information and be prepared to extend the contract for
construction management services to McDonough Bolyard Peck (MBP) at the September 15, 2026 meeting.
DATA SOURCE:
Daniel Keever, Superintendent
Marcellus Snipes, Senior Director for Operations

items.title: Review of Calendar Year 2027 School Board Meeting Dates
items.body:
TOPIC:
Review of Calendar Year 2027 School Board Meeting Dates
BACKGROUND:
Per Policy BCA, School Board Organizational Meeting, the board will hold an organizational meeting annually
in January and establish its regular meeting schedule for the following year.
It has been determined that more advance planning and notice of the meeting schedule increases efficiency
and improves communication for board members, staff, and the community. Therefore, a proposed school
board meeting schedule for calendar year 2027 is being presented for review by the board, with the goal of
approval on September 15, 2026.
RATIONALE:
The Code of Virginia, § 22.1-72, reads: "Each school board shall hold its annual organizational meeting for the
purpose of establishing its regular meeting schedule for the ensuing year..."
To remain complaint with state code, during the January Organizational Meeting the board will have the
opportunity to confirm or amend the planned meeting dates for calendar year 2027.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
The school board may also hold special meetings when necessary.
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board review the proposed meeting schedule for calendar year 2027 and
be prepared to vote at the meeting on September 15, 2026.

items.title: Redistricting Update: Steering Committee Map Recommendation
items.body:
TOPIC:
Redistricting Update: Steering Committee Map Recommendation
BACKGROUND:
Many school buildings in WJCC Schools, specifically at the elementary level, are at capacity. To accommodate
student population, eight of nine WJCC elementary schools have portable classrooms (trailers) on site. With the
anticipated August 2027 occupancy of two new pre-k centers, the school division must also consider the best and
most efficient way to utilize elementary space that will be available when pre-k students are located in the new pre-k
spaces as the current pre-k program is housed in five elementary schools. The shift will leave some elementary
spaces unoccupied while other spaces remain at or over capacity. Engaging in conversation on school zones also
allows the school division to consider boundaries, feeder pattern alignment, efficiencies and effective delivery at the
secondary level.
RATIONALE:
The Redistricting Steering Committee released draft attendance zone maps for each level on May 12, 2026, and
revisions were presented on August 4, 2026. Community members have engaged in a second feedback process.
The Redistricting Steering Committee’s map recommendation will be presented to Dr. Keever.

items.title: WJCC United Transition Roadmap
items.body:
TOPIC:
WJCC United Transition Roadmap
BACKGROUND:
Many WJCC school buildings, particularly at the elementary level, are at or near capacity. Eight of the
division’s nine elementary schools currently use portable classrooms to accommodate student enrollment. At
the same time, the anticipated opening of two new pre-K centers in August 2027 will relocate pre-K programs
currently housed in five elementary schools, creating available instructional space in some buildings while
others are projected to remain at or above capacity. Reviewing attendance zones provides an opportunity to
more effectively utilize available capacity across the division while also considering feeder pattern alignment,
transportation and operational efficiencies, and the effective delivery of programs and services at both the
elementary and secondary levels.
An interdepartmental leadership team has been established to proactively prepare for the 2027-2028 school
year should the School Board approve new attendance boundaries. The team will coordinate a thoughtful
implementation that addresses both operational needs and the human impact of change on students, families,
employees, and school communities.
RATIONALE:
The WJCC United Transition Roadmap will provide a coordinated framework for supporting students, families,
employees, and school communities should new attendance boundaries be approved for the 2027-2028 school
year. Organized around four areas of focus (Student Experience, Employee Experience & Team Transitions,
Family Engagement, and Communications & Logistics), the roadmap will ensure division leadership addresses
both the operational requirements and the human impact of redistricting through proactive planning, clear
communication, intentional engagement, and targeted transition supports. This initial presentation will provide
an overview of the focus areas and phases for implementation. Ongoing updates will be provided as additional
decisions are made.

N/A

N/A

items.body:
TOPIC:
Review Revisions to Policy IA, Instructional Goals and Objectives
BACKGROUND:
The Code of Virginia, § 22.1-253.13-7, Standard 7 requires that each local school board shall maintain and
follow up-to-date policies. All school board policies shall be reviewed and revised as needed.
RATIONALE:
Staff comments/recommendation:
• Policy last revised August 2024
• Aligned revisions with the VSBA Model Policy, which went through a substantial rewrite in May 2026 to
remove unnecessary language that is incorporated in other policies, including the new policy IK.
• Revised language clarifies and strengthens the policy
o Line 7 – remove “develops and implements”, add “is committed to providing”
o Line 8 – add “comprehensive” and “consistent with the”
o Line 9 – add “requirements of Virginia law and”, “meets or exceeds” and remove “aligned” and
“to”
o Lines 10-12 – add “Students are expected to achieve the educational objectives established by
the school division at appropriate age and grade levels.”
o Line 14 – add “division’s”
o Line 15 – add “skills of communication including”
o Line 20 – add “U.S. and world”
o Lines 33-36 – add VSBA recommended statement regarding the superintendent’s expectations
for implementation
• Legal and cross references updated
• Attorney reviewed and approved changes
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board continue to update/revise their Policy Manual in accordance with
state and federal laws.
DATA SOURCE:
Robin Ford, Chief Academic Officer

items.title: Review Revisions to Policy IGAG, Teaching about Drugs, Alcohol and Tobacco IGAG Redline - IGAG Teaching About Drugs, Alcohol and Tobacco
items.body:
TOPIC:
Review Revisions to Policy IGAG, Teaching about Drugs, Alcohol and Tobacco
BACKGROUND:
The Code of Virginia, § 22.1-253.13-7, Standard 7 requires that each local school board shall maintain and
follow up-to-date policies. All school board policies shall be reviewed and revised as needed.
RATIONALE:
Staff comments/recommendation:
• Last revised August 2022
• Reviewed associated VSBA Model Policy, which added additional language requirements from Va.
Code regarding screen time/time spent on electronic devices to required instruction
• Recommend changing policy title to align with the VSBA, and be more representative of policy content:
“Teaching about Drugs, Alcohol, Tobacco, Gambling, and Electronic Devices”
• Line 11 – add “hemp products intended for smoking”
• Lines 14-15 - add “time spent using electronic devices such as computers, cell phones, and other smart
devices and the addictive potential thereof”
• Lines 17-20 – add VSBA recommended statement regarding a program of instruction on opioid
overdose prevention
• Legal and cross references updated
• Attorney reviewed and approved changes
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A

N/A

1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.

state and federal laws.
DATA SOURCE:
Robin Ford, Chief Academic Officer
Adam Otstot, Coordinator for Health/PE & Athletics

items.title: Approval of Personnel Actions
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
9/1/2026
TOPIC:
Approve Personnel Actions as Presented
BACKGROUND:
Personnel Actions list Appointments, Change in Status, Reassignments, Separations, Stipends, etc. of
employees. The positions listed are authorized in the 2026-2027 budget and are required as outlined, grantfunded, or are mandated by federal or state law. Funds are available for any new positions listed.
RATIONALE:
The listing of all WJCCPS Personnel Actions supports Policy BBA, School Board Powers and Duties, which
includes as a major responsibility "To employ teachers, and other school personnel, upon the recommendation
of the superintendent."
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
Refer to Personnel Actions listed.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the Personnel Actions as presented
2. Approve the Personnel Actions with amendments
3. Do not approve the Personnel Actions
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends that the Personnel Actions be approved as presented.
DATA SOURCE:
Emily Haywood, Chief Human Resources Officer
RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Move to approve personnel actions as presented.
